Dylan T: Heads-up — saw nondeterministic top_p behavior during the quantized model bring-up evals in CI (job 8902). Runs with identical seed + config produced different sampling distributions across shards.
Eva L: uh oh. any quick repro?
Dylan T: Yep. Minimal repro attached in the job artifacts. TL;DR: when we stream tokens back and interleave multiple small batches, top_p seems to be computed on different cumulative probs per shard so top candidates differ.
Maya R: that sounds like the shard-local softmax/normalization got different precision or ordering? Could be fp16 sum order noise, but shouldn't change which tokens are in top_p bucket consistently.
Samir K: Can you paste the log snippet where two shards disagree?
Dylan T: sure:
```
# shard 0 probs (top 6): [0.22,0.18,0.16,0.14,0.10,0.08] -> cum [0.22,0.40,0.56,0.70,0.80,0.88]
# shard 1 probs (top 6): [0.21,0.19,0.17,0.14,0.09,0.08] -> cum [0.21,0.40,0.57,0.71,0.80,0.88]
# top_p=0.9 -> chosen sets differ (shard0 picks 6, shard1 picks 6 but different ordering)
```
Maya R: those look super close. If we rely on deterministic tie-breaking, ordering variance could flip which token passes the top_p cutoff.
Len G: Also worth checking RNG assignment: we currently instantiate a generator per worker using time-based seed + worker_id. If workers are reused across requests the seed can be polluted.
Dylan T: I reproduced with single-run local harness: set seed=12345, run 1000 eval ex, got ~2.3% of examples with differing outputs between runs. Root cause looks like interleaved sampling when continuous-batching merges unfinished prefix requests.
Samir K: Maybe the sampler uses a shared RNG and calls are interleaved? We had a TODO about making sampler coroutines reentrant.
Eva L: Proposed short fixes: 1) assign a per-request Philox counter-based RNG (stateless) so ordering doesn't matter, or 2) make top_p selection use stable sort + deterministic tie-breaker.
Maya R: I lean to (1) for long-term correctness. Philox/Threefry style counter-RNG gives reproducibility even under concurrency. Faster to prototype: wrap sampling in a request-scoped RNG seeded from (global_seed, request_id).
Dylan T: I'll try that. Quick patch I tested locally:
```
# pseudo
rng = PhiloxCounter(seed=global_seed, counter=request.seq)
probs = softmax(logits)
topk = stable_argsort(probs)  # stable
selected = take_while_cumsum(topk, probs, top_p, rng)
```
Worked: two independent runs now match for 5k samples.
CI-bot: Job 8902 failed — reproduce artifact uploaded: https://ci/repro/8902/artifacts
Len G: Nice. Can we add a unit test that simulates concurrent worker reuse and checks deterministic outputs for fixed seeds?
Samir K: Yes add a small integration test to eval-runner/tests/test_determinism.py that spins up N worker threads and compares outputs across runs. Make it fast and mark as flaky-gate?
Eva L: Also add a perf guard — Philox per-request shouldn't slow things significantly, but let's run perf once. If overhead is big, we can pool stateless counter increments.
Dylan T: I'll open a PR with the Philox change + test + CI job update. Assigning to @Maya R for review.
Maya R: ack. I'll review tomorrow morning. If green, let's promote to canary for Dedicated run and monitor eval regression dashboard for false positives. :thumbsup:
Dylan T: thanks all — filing follow-ups: GH-#4827 (deterministic sampler), GH-#4828 (determinism test), and CI job tweak.
